true_positives.golden_comment: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
`<%- end if %>` is a typo that only compiles by accident

The closing tag of the header conditional is `<%- end if %>` instead of `<%- end %>`. Erubis emits `end if \n` followed by the next generated statement, so Ruby parses it as `(if ... else ... end) if @output_buffer.safe_append='...'` — a modifier-if whose condition is the whitespace-append statement for the following text node. It happens to be truthy so the template renders, but the output ordering is now dependent on surrounding whitespace and any reformatting of the template (e.g. removing the blank line, or an expression tag immediately following) turns this into a `SyntaxError` that 500s the whole embed endpoint. Replace with `<%- end %>`.

false_positives.candidate:
Disqus import silently drops the --category option and original topic timestamps

The `category` method_option was removed and the topic is now created via `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, which no longer passes `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])` or a category. Imported threads will all appear in the uncategorized category with the import time as their creation date (and therefore sort as brand-new), and anyone invoking the task with `-c` will get a Thor 'unknown option' error. If this is intentional it should be mentioned; otherwise thread `created_at`/`category` through `import_remote`/`import` opts to `PostCreator`.

Every retrieval of an unknown URL synchronously re-polls and re-imports the entire RSS feed

When `feed_polling_enabled` is on, `perform_retrieve` runs `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline, which downloads and parses the whole feed and calls `TopicEmbed.import` for every item (each doing a DB lookup, SHA1, Nokogiri parse) before falling back to `fetch_http`. Because `embed/best` enqueues a retrieval for every unknown `embed_url` and the throttle is per-URL, a handful of visitors hitting distinct not-yet-embedded pages (or an attacker varying the query string) causes repeated full feed re-imports on the Sidekiq workers. Consider only consulting the already-scheduled hourly poll results, or at minimum throttling the feed poll itself globally.

Feed HTML is stored and rendered completely unsanitized

`CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content)` is passed straight to `TopicEmbed.import`, which stores it as a `raw_html` post; `Post#cook` returns `raw` verbatim for that cook method, so no sanitizer (PrettyText/Sanitize) ever runs on it. Unlike `import_remote`, which at least passes content through Readability's tag/attribute whitelist, the RSS path lets `<script>`, event handlers, `javascript:` hrefs, iframes etc. from the feed land in `cooked` and execute for every visitor of the forum and of the embed iframe. A compromised blog, a third-party/aggregated feed, or an author-submitted post on a multi-author site becomes site-wide stored XSS on the forum. Run feed content through the same whitelist used for Readability (or Sanitize) before storing.

Key authorization and parsing paths are untested

The controller spec only covers 'no referer'; there is no test that a referer on a *different* host is rejected, which is the actual security property of `ensure_embeddable`. Likewise `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb` never exercises `poll_feed` itself (nil `content`, non-http `link` falling back to `id`), and `spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb` has no cases for protocol-relative URLs, non-default ports, or the update path when the post has been deleted — all of which have concrete bugs in this PR. Add tests for referer-host mismatch, a feed item without `content`, and `absolutize_urls` with `//host/path` input.

New gems only added to Gemfile_rails4.lock; Rails 3 lockfile not updated

`ruby-readability` and `simple-rss` are added unconditionally to the Gemfile, but only `Gemfile_rails4.lock` was regenerated. Booting with `RAILS3=1` resolves against `Gemfile.lock`, which no longer matches the Gemfile; in deployment/frozen mode `bundle install` fails, and in normal mode the lockfile is silently rewritten with potentially different versions. Either regenerate `Gemfile.lock` as well or scope the gems to the rails4 branch.

No per-item error handling: one bad item (or the post rate limiter) aborts the whole feed

The `rss.items.each` loop calls `TopicEmbed.import` with no rescue. Any exception for a single item — malformed `URI`, nil title, the `PostCreator` spam/NOT NULL failure described elsewhere, or `RateLimiter::LimitExceeded` — propagates, `sidekiq_options retry: false` means the job is not retried, and all remaining items are skipped. In particular `Post` declares `rate_limit` (`rate_limit_create_post`, `max_topics_per_day: 20`); unless `embed_by_username` is staff, importing a feed with more than 20 items raises `LimitExceeded` partway through on every run, and `rate_limit_create_post` (5s between posts) will trip on consecutive items. The Disqus thor task explicitly calls `RateLimiter.disable` for the same reason; the job should do likewise (or use a staff-only importer) and wrap each item in a rescue that logs and continues.

Port is omitted/added based on hardcoded 80/443 instead of the scheme's default port

`prefix << ":#{uri.port}" if uri.port != 80 && uri.port != 443` drops the port for `https://host:80/` and `http://host:443/`, producing a prefix that points at the wrong port for those (unusual but valid) URLs. Use `uri.port != uri.default_port` so the port is kept exactly when it differs from the scheme default.

When a `TopicEmbed` row exists, `embed.post` is used unconditionally. `Post` includes `Trashable`, so a post that has been deleted (trashed) is excluded by the default scope and `embed.post` returns nil; `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!` then raises `NoMethodError` on the next feed poll or retrieve, and since `PollFeed` has no per-item error handling this aborts the whole feed run every hour until the row is removed by hand. Throttle key set with SETNX then EXPIRE non-atomically

`$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by a separate `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)` is not atomic. If the worker dies or the Redis connection drops between the two calls, the key persists with no TTL and `retrieved_recently?` returns true forever for that URL, so non-staff visitors can never trigger retrieval of that embed again. Use `SET key 1 NX EX 60` (or `setex` inside a MULTI) so the TTL is applied in the same operation.

Unauthenticated users can trigger topic creation for arbitrary URLs on the embeddable host

`EmbedController#best` is reachable without login (`current_user` may be nil) and the only gate is a `Referer` header whose host equals `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`; `Referer` is trivially spoofed with curl. There is no per-client rate limit, no check that the URL path is one the site owner intends to embed, and no dedupe on fetched content. Consequence: anonymous topic flooding / forum spam and an outbound-fetch amplifier.

`post.present?` is the wrong success check for PostCreator; failures surface as NOT NULL violations and abort the import

`PostCreator#create` returns the unsaved `Post` object (with `errors` populated) when it rolls back, e.g. when `rollback_if_host_spam_detected` fires. `post.present?` is therefore true even on failure, and the code proceeds to `TopicEmbed.create!(post_id: post.id)` with `post.id == nil`, which hits the `post_id NOT NULL` constraint and raises a `PG::NotNullViolation` out of `import`. This is not a remote edge case: the configured `embed_by_username` user is typically a freshly created bot account at trust level 0, every imported post links to the same external host (the 'Imported from' footer alone guarantees this), and `Post#has_host_spam?` blocks TL0 users after `newuser_spam_host_threshold` (3) posts to the same domain. After the third import every subsequent import raises, the hourly `PollFeed` run aborts on the first item, and moderators receive spam-blocked PMs. Note also that the inner `Post.transaction` in `PostCreator` swallows `ActiveRecord::Rollback` because it is nested in `Topic.transaction` without `requires_new`, so relying on the rollback to clean up is fragile. Check `post.persisted?`/`post.errors.blank?` and either bypass or handle spam/rate-limit checks for the importer user.

absolutize_urls mangles protocol-relative URLs (//cdn.example.com/...) Both the `` and `` branches treat anything starting with `/` as site-relative and rewrite it to `"#{prefix}/#{href.sub(/^\/+/, '')}"`. A protocol-relative URL such as `//cdn.example.com/img.png` (very common in WordPress and other feeds) therefore becomes `http://embeddable-host/cdn.example.com/img.png`, which is a broken link/image in every imported post. Only rewrite when the value starts with a single `/` (or use `URI.join(url, href)` which handles all relative forms correctly).

import_remote uses Kernel#open on a semi-trusted URL with no scheme check, timeout, size limit or redirect restriction

`TopicEmbed.import_remote` calls `open(url).read` (Kernel#open via open-uri) before `import` performs its `^https?://` check, so for the `TopicRetriever` path only the *host* of the URL has been validated. open-uri will follow HTTP redirects to any host, so a page on the embeddable host (or an attacker who can place redirects there) can make the forum fetch internal/other-host resources; there is also no read timeout and no size cap, so a slow or huge response ties up or exhausts a Sidekiq worker. Validate the scheme up front, use an explicit HTTP client with timeouts, a maximum body size, and either disable redirects or re-validate the host on each hop.

true_positives.golden_comment: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
align-items mixin forwards the modern keyword unchanged to legacy prefixes and emits a non-existent `-ms-align-items` property

`-webkit-box-align` (2009 model) and `-ms-flex-align` (IE10 2012 draft) accept `start`/`end`, not `flex-start`/`flex-end`; the mixin passes `$alignment` through verbatim, so any future `@include align-items(flex-start)` silently produces invalid declarations for those engines (only `center`/`baseline`, the values used today, happen to coincide). Additionally `-ms-align-items` was never implemented by any IE version (IE11 uses unprefixed `align-items`), so that line is dead output in every compiled stylesheet. Either map the keywords inside the mixin or drop the legacy prefixes to avoid a mixin that looks portable but isn't. (Same class of issue in `order()`: `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` is 1-based while `order` is 0-based, so identical values do not produce identical relative ordering against default items.)

.extra-info-wrapper as a flex item has `min-width: auto`, so long topic titles will push .panel out of the header

Now that `.contents` is a flex container, `.extra-info-wrapper` (which holds the docked topic title and category badge) becomes a flex item. Flex items default to `min-width: auto`, meaning they refuse to shrink below their content's min-content width. The wrapper gets `order(2)` but no `flex: 1 1 auto` / `min-width: 0` / `overflow: hidden`, so a long topic title (especially one with `white-space: nowrap`, as applied to `.badge-wrapper`) will widen the item and push `.panel` outside the header or wrap the row, instead of truncating as the previous float layout allowed. Add `min-width: 0; flex: 1;` (with `overflow: hidden`/ellipsis as desired) to the wrapper.

Float-based header layout removed with no fallback for browsers without any flexbox support

`.title { float: left }` and `.panel { float: right }` were deleted and replaced solely by flexbox on `.contents`. Browsers with no flexbox implementation at all (IE9 and older, Opera Mini) will now render `.title`, `.extra-info-wrapper` and `.panel` as stacked block elements, breaking the header entirely rather than degrading. If any such browser is still in the support matrix the floats should be kept as a fallback (flexbox ignores floats on flex items, so keeping them is harmless for flex-capable browsers).

PR title claims a performance optimization; the change is a layout refactor and the description is a placeholder

The PR is titled "Optimize header layout performance with flexbox mixins" but nothing in the diff affects rendering/scrolling performance — it swaps float positioning for flexbox and adds vendor-prefix mixins, which if anything emits more CSS. The description is just "Test 5". A maintainer reading the history will be misled about why the header, small-action and badge layouts changed; the title/description should describe the actual change (float → flexbox layout, vendor-prefix mixins) and note the visual changes (removed bullet margin, small-action spacing).

Removing paragraph margins in .custom-message collapses spacing between multi-paragraph messages `.small-action .small-action-desc .custom-message p` had `margin: 5px 0` and now has `margin: 0`. Custom close/archive/pin messages can contain multiple paragraphs (the message is cooked markdown), so consecutive `

` elements will now render with no vertical separation and read as a single run-on block. If the intent was only to remove the outer top/bottom spacing for the flex centering, use `p + p { margin-top: 5px }` or zero only `:first-child`/`:last-child` margins.

Right-alignment of .panel relies on `margin-left: auto`, which the legacy `-webkit-box` model emitted by the mixin does not honor

The `flexbox()` mixin deliberately emits `display: -webkit-box` / `-moz-box` for legacy WebKit/Gecko engines (Android stock browser < 4.4, Safari < 6.1, old Chrome). In the 2009 box model, auto margins are not used for distribution and `float` is ignored on box children, so with `float: right` removed and only `margin-left: auto` added, `.panel` (the icons/login buttons) will sit directly after the site title instead of at the right edge of the header on exactly the browsers the prefixes are meant to support. `.small-action` is turned into a flex container via `@include flexbox()`, which makes `.topic-avatar`, `.small-action-desc` and `button` flex items. The CSS Flexbox spec states that `float` has no effect on flex items, so the `float: right` left on `button` (and `float: left` on `.topic-avatar`) no longer does anything. Because `.small-action-desc` has no `flex: 1`/width and the button has no `margin-left: auto`, the action button (e.g. the close/archive toggle) will now render immediately after the description text instead of at the right edge of the row — a visible layout regression for every small-action post. `getClient` unconditionally POSTs to `login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` and performs a `prisma.credential.update` every time `SalesforceCalendarService` is constructed (which happens for every booking/availability flow), regardless of whether the stored token is still valid—previously jsforce refreshed lazily. This adds a network round-trip and a DB write per instantiation and will hit Salesforce token-endpoint rate limits. Moreover, the `jsforce.Connection` is still built with `credentialKey.access_token` / `credentialKey.instance_url` (the pre-refresh values) rather than `accessTokenParsed.data`, so the freshly obtained token isn't even used. Also `response.statusText !== "OK"` is fragile (HTTP/2 responses have an empty statusText); check `response.ok`.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Webhook secret compared with `!==` and no HTTP method/body-shape error handling

The shared secret header is compared with plain `!==`, which is not constant-time and leaks timing information about the secret; use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers. The handler also accepts any HTTP method (a GET with a header would try to `parse(req.body)` and throw) and lets `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse`, `symmetricDecrypt`, and `JSON.parse` throw unhandled, producing 500s with stack details instead of a 400. Restrict to POST and wrap validation/decryption in proper error responses.

false_positives.candidate:
Helper throws on invalid response, making callers' `!success` branches dead and changing Office365 error behavior

`parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws `"Invalid refreshed tokens were returned"` when validation fails, so the `if (!parsedToken.success)` checks in `zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts` and `salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts` can never execute. For Office365 this silently changes behavior: the previous code logged the Zod error together with Microsoft's raw response and continued; now the diagnostic logging was deleted and the refresh throws, leaving operators with no information about why Microsoft's response was rejected. Either return the failed result and let callers handle it, or keep the diagnostic logging in the helper.

No tests for the new webhook or the shared refresh helpers

The PR adds a new authenticated API endpoint that writes third-party credentials to the DB and two helpers (`refreshOAuthTokens`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse`) that are now on the token-refresh path of ten integrations, yet ships no unit or integration tests (the PR checklist explicitly says none were added). Several of the defects above (SafeParse wrapper stored as key, broken computed-key schema, Response vs SDK shape mismatch, missing prisma import) would have been caught by even a basic test of each helper's output shape and of one adapter's refresh flow in both sync and non-sync modes.

Request to the self-hoster's credential sync endpoint carries no authentication

The POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` in the body with no secret/signature header (e.g. `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` under `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME`, which the inbound webhook already requires). The endpoint returns live OAuth access tokens for arbitrary user ids, so the self-hoster is forced to either leave it unauthenticated (anyone who can reach it can obtain any user's third-party tokens by guessing numeric ids) or rely on network-level controls. The outgoing request should include the shared secret so the endpoint can verify the caller.

Webhook upserts by (userId, appId) and will silently overwrite an arbitrary credential when a user has several for the same app

Cal.com allows multiple credentials per user for the same app (e.g. several Google Calendar accounts, each a separate `Credential` row with `appId: "google-calendar"`). The handler does `findFirst({ where: { userId, appId } })` with no ordering and overwrites whichever row is returned, so a sync for one connected account can clobber the keys of a different one, breaking that calendar connection. It also never considers team-owned credentials. The payload should identify the target credential (e.g. a credential id or an external account identifier), or the handler should refuse/branch when more than one match exists.

Zoom sends app slug "zoomvideo" to the sync endpoint, but the app's slug is "zoom"

The inbound webhook (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`) looks apps up by their store slug, and Zoom's slug is `zoom` (see `zoomvideo/api/callback.ts` creating the credential with `appId: "zoom"`). The refresh path, however, calls `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoomvideo", ...)`. A self-hoster keying their endpoint by the same slugs they use for the webhook will not recognize `zoomvideo`, so Zoom token refresh via sync fails. Use the canonical slug `zoom` to match the rest of the system.

`prisma` is used but never imported in Salesforce CalendarService

The new refresh block in `getClient` calls `await prisma.credential.update(...)`, but this file has no `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma"` (imports are only jsforce, rrule, zod, lib helpers and types). This is a type-check error and, if it slipped through, a `ReferenceError: prisma is not defined` at runtime on every Salesforce service instantiation, making the Salesforce integration unusable.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: macOS-specific sed syntax with empty string after -i flag will fail on Linux systems
true_positives.matched_candidate:
`sed -i ''` is BSD/macOS-only syntax; script fails on Linux

`sed -i '' -E "s|...|...|" "$ENV_FILE"` uses the BSD form of in-place editing. On GNU sed (Linux, which is what most contributors and CI use) `-i ''` is parsed as `-i` with no suffix followed by `''` as the sed script and `-E` as a filename, producing `sed: can't read -E: No such file or directory` and leaving `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` unchanged. Use a portable approach (e.g. `sed -i.bak ... && rm "$ENV_FILE.bak"`, or detect the platform).

true_positives.golden_comment: Throwing a generic Error for authentication failures results in a 500 response in tRPC. Instead, it should return a structured TRPCError with an appropriate code, such as FORBIDDEN, to accurately reflect the error type.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Access-denied/not-found case throws a plain Error, surfacing as a 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR

When the credential does not belong to the caller (or does not exist) the handler throws `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. tRPC maps non-`TRPCError` exceptions to `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR`, so a legitimate authorization failure is reported to the client as a server error (and will be logged/alerted as one). Use `new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" })` or `"FORBIDDEN"` as the rest of the viewer routers do.

true_positives.golden_comment: Date is formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of using the user's locale from useLocale, which can lead to incorrect date representation for users in different locales.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Cache timestamp is hard-coded to the en-US locale

`new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` ignores the user's locale even though the surrounding strings are translated via `useLocale`. Non-English users will see a US-formatted date (M/D/YY, 12-hour clock) inside a localized sentence. `useLocale()` exposes the current locale (and the codebase already has dayjs/timeFormat helpers) — use it instead of the literal.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.

false_positives.candidate:
CalendarCacheRepository is instantiated directly, bypassing the calendar-cache feature flag

Elsewhere the repository is obtained through `CalendarCache.init(...)`, which returns `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` when the `calendar-cache` feature is disabled. Here `new CalendarCacheRepository()` is used unconditionally, so every `connectedCalendars` query performs an extra `groupBy` on `CalendarCache` and may surface stale cache status for deployments/teams that have the feature turned off (the mock, which this PR also updated, is never reached from this path).

ENV_FILE is resolved relative to the caller's cwd, not the script location

`ENV_FILE="../.env"` assumes the script is executed from inside `scripts/`. Running it the conventional way from the repo root (`./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh`) resolves to a `.env` one directory *above* the repository; the script then prints a warning, `touch`es a stray file outside the repo and writes `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` there, so the app never picks it up. Resolve relative to the script: `ENV_FILE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)/.env"`. Additionally, `cleanup` always `exit 0`, so the failure paths (rate limit hit, URL not extracted) report success to the caller.

Extra bulk UPDATE on every webhook refresh writes a field nothing reads

`fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` is invoked from the Google webhook handler on every push notification. The new `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` issues an `UPDATE SelectedCalendar ... WHERE credentialId = ?` solely to bump `@updatedAt` across all selected calendars for that credential (including event-type-level rows). The PR description itself notes the frontend does not consume `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` and uses `CalendarCache.updatedAt` instead. This is a redundant write amplifying webhook load with no consumer, and an empty `data: {}` relies on Prisma's implicit `@updatedAt` behaviour for `updateMany`, which is non-obvious to future readers. Remove it (or document the consumer if one is intended).

Migration header contradicts the statement and legacy rows will show the migration time as 'last updated'

The header comment says the column is added "without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty", but the statement right below adds it with `DEFAULT NOW()`, so the warning is stale/misleading. More importantly, every pre-existing `CalendarCache` row is stamped with the migration run time, so after deploy the new UI will display "Last updated: <deploy time>" for all legacy caches regardless of how old their contents actually are. Consider back-filling from a meaningful value (e.g. `expiresAt - interval '30 days'`, which mirrors `CACHING_TIME`) or fix the comment to explain the inaccuracy.

No tests for the new deleteCache handler or getCacheStatusByCredentialIds

The PR adds a destructive mutation with an ownership check and a new repository aggregation, but no unit/integration tests: there is nothing asserting that a user cannot delete another user's cache, that the cache rows are actually removed, or that `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` returns the max `updatedAt` per credential. The PR description itself notes local verification was not possible. At minimum add handler tests for the forbidden/success paths and a repository test for the groupBy mapping.

UserWithCalendars now requires `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` on selected calendars although neither is used

The `Pick<SelectedCalendar, ...>` for `allSelectedCalendars`/`userLevelSelectedCalendars` was widened to require `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId`, but nothing in this file (or in `connectedCalendars.handler.ts`) reads those fields — the UI gets its timestamp from `CalendarCache.updatedAt`. This tightens the public input type of `getConnectedDestinationCalendarsAndEnsureDefaultsInDb`, which is re-exported for `@calcom/platform-libraries`/API v2, so any caller that builds the user object with an explicit `select` of only `externalId/integration/eventTypeId` will now fail type-checking for no functional benefit. Either drop the additions or actually use them.

`dev:cron` switched to `npx tsx` but `tsx` is not a declared dependency

The script now runs `npx tsx cron-tester.ts` while `tsx` is not listed in `dependencies`/`devDependencies` (only `ts-node` is). `npx` will try to download the latest `tsx` at invocation time, which is non-reproducible, fails offline, and bypasses yarn's lockfile. Either add `tsx` as a devDependency and call it directly, or keep `ts-node`. This change is also unrelated to the PR's stated scope.

deleteCache mutation never invalidates connectedCalendars query, leaving stale cache status in the UI

The `deleteCacheMutation` only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` prop. Unlike `disconnectMutation` (which invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` in `onSettled`), nothing refetches the connected calendars query after the cache rows are deleted. `cacheUpdatedAt` comes from that query, so after a successful deletion the dropdown continues to show "Cache Status / Last updated: ..." and the "Delete cached data" item until the page is reloaded. In `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper` `onChanged` is an optional prop that is frequently undefined, so the fallback does not help. Add `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()` in `onSettled`/`onSuccess` of the delete-cache mutation.

getCacheStatusByCredentialIds reports expired cache rows as live cache status

The `groupBy` has no `expiresAt: { gte: now }` filter, whereas every read path (`getCachedAvailability`) only serves rows whose `expiresAt` is in the future. A credential whose cache entries have all expired (e.g. the Google watch channel lapsed a month ago) will still be shown in the UI as having a cache with a "Last updated" timestamp and a "Delete cached data" action, even though no cache is actually being served. This defeats the purpose of a cache status indicator. Filter on `expiresAt >= new Date()` (or return both values so the UI can show expired state).

`StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` was changed to return `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]`, but its docstring still reads "returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`". Implementers reading the docstring will get the wrong contract; it should describe the dict keyed by group key.

true_positives.golden_comment: Wrong value `6` passed for `group_2` occurrence — the data packet specifies `"group_2": 10`. Should be `10` to accurately reflect the test scenario, which will ensure the test produces the correct occurrence data.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Expected occurrence in TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe is built with the wrong group key

In `TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe`, the expected `IssueOccurrence` is built via `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", 6, PriorityLevel.HIGH)`, but `evaluate_group_key_value` is invoked with `group_key="group_key"`. `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` uses `handler.build_fingerprint(group_key)`, so the expected fingerprint is `["<id>:val1"]` while the handler will produce `["<id>:group_key"]`. `IssueOccurrence` is a frozen dataclass with field-wise equality, so `DetectorEvaluationResult.__eq__` will compare these as unequal and the assertion `== expected_result` cannot pass as written (or, if it does pass, it indicates equality is not comparing what the test intends). Stale TODO comment about becoming a stateful detector

The comment `# TODO: This will be a stateful detector when we build that abstraction` is now inaccurate: the class directly subclasses `StatefulDetectorHandler` in this PR, so the abstraction exists and is already being used. The TODO should be removed or replaced with one describing the actual remaining work (implementing the abstract hooks).

true_positives.golden_comment: In the SpanFlusher flush loop, metric tags inconsistently use 'shard' (e.g., in spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes) and 'shards' (in spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce) for the same shard identifier value. This prevents correct metric aggregation across flush stages — dashboards and alerts filtering by tag 'shard' will miss data tagged as 'shards' and vice versa.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Inconsistent metric tag names: "shard" vs "shards"

`spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` are tagged with `{"shard": shard_tag}` while `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` on the same code path uses `{"shards": shard_tag}`, and `spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy` uses `shard` with a single int. The same comma-joined value is emitted under two different tag keys, which makes dashboards/queries inconsistent. Pick one tag name.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because flusher processes are created via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, they are instances of multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess, which on POSIX is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process, so this isinstance check will always be false and hung processes won't be killed here.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) is False for spawn-context processes, so hung flushers are never killed

Processes are created via `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process`, which yields `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess`. `SpawnProcess` subclasses `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess`, not `multiprocessing.Process` (= `multiprocessing.context.Process`), so `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` evaluates to False. In `_ensure_processes_alive` this means `process.kill()` is never called when a process is detected as hung (`cause == "hang"`). Before this PR `kill()` was invoked unconditionally. Consequence: a hung-but-alive flusher is leaked and a second process is started for the same shards; if the old one resumes, two flushers concurrently run `flush_segments`/`done_flush_segments` on the same Redis shards, which can produce duplicate segments to buffered-segments and double the Redis load. Use `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess)` (or `not isinstance(process, threading.Thread)`) instead. The same wrong check in `join()` (line 346) means `terminate()` is also never called there.

true_positives.golden_comment: Breaking out of the loop when the deadline has elapsed can skip terminating remaining flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown; consider ensuring termination is attempted even if the deadline is exceeded.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
join() stops terminating remaining processes once the deadline passes

In `join()`, when the deadline has elapsed the loop does `break`, which skips `process.terminate()` for every process not yet visited. Previously the single process was always terminated after the wait. With several flusher processes, any that haven't exited by the join timeout are left running (only the `stopped` flag is set, which a hung process ignores). The `break` should be removed so each remaining process still gets `terminate()` called (the inner `while` already respects the deadline).

false_negatives.golden_comment: The test_basic function in test_consumer.py uses a monkeypatched time.sleep that returns immediately, but then calls time.sleep(0.1) expecting it to actually wait.
Sleep in test_consumer.py won’t actually wait because time.sleep was monkeypatched above; consider restoring sleep or using a different sync to ensure the flusher has time to process.

false_positives.candidate:
Docstring claims one process per shard, but default is a single process

The class docstring says "Creates one process per shard for parallel processing", but `max_processes` caps the count, and the CLI option `--flusher-processes` defaults to 1, so in the default deployment all shards share one process. The docstring should describe the `max_processes` parameter and the shard-to-process distribution instead.

No test covers the real multiprocess path or process restart

Both new/updated tests pass `produce_to_pipe`, which forces the `threading.Thread` code path. The actual `mp_context.Process` branch (pickling the per-shard buffer, `run_with_initialized_sentry`, `is_alive`/`kill`/`terminate` handling in `_ensure_processes_alive` and `join`) is never exercised, which is exactly where the `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` bug lives. `test_flusher_processes_limit` also only asserts the total shard count; it does not check that shards are disjoint across processes or that a dead process is recreated for the same shards. Adding a test that spawns at least one real process (or a restart test with a thread that exits early) would catch regressions here.

Redis memory info is fetched once per flusher process instead of once per cluster

`SpansBuffer.get_memory_info()` returns memory usage for every node of the Redis cluster, not just the buffer's shards. `submit()` now calls it for each per-process `SpansBuffer` and sums the results. With N flusher processes this issues N times as many `INFO memory` calls to every Redis node on every submit, and `used`/`available` are each over-counted N times (the ratio happens to survive, but the values are wrong if anyone logs/reports them). Since the check is cluster-wide, it should run once (e.g. on a single buffer) rather than per process.

true_positives.golden_comment: Race condition: Multiple concurrent requests could pass the device count check simultaneously and create devices beyond the limit. Consider using a database transaction or lock.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Count-then-insert is not atomic; concurrent new devices can exceed the configured limit

`CreateOrUpdateDevice` runs `CountDevices` in one DB session and the insert/upsert in a separate `WithDbSession` call, with no transaction or row locking. If several previously-unseen devices authenticate concurrently (or across multiple Grafana instances, which share the table but not the local cache), each sees `count < deviceLimit` and all of them insert, so the number of active devices can exceed `device_limit` by the degree of concurrency. If the limit is meant to be a hard cap (it blocks authentication), the check and insert should be performed in a single transaction, or the insert should be made conditional in SQL.

true_positives.golden_comment: Anonymous authentication now fails entirely if anonDeviceService.TagDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached. Previously, device tagging was asynchronous and non-blocking. This change prevents anonymous users from authenticating when the device limit is reached.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unauthenticated callers can exhaust the device limit with arbitrary device IDs and lock out anonymous access for 30 days

`X-Grafana-Device-Id` is a client-supplied header with no validation, and each distinct value creates a row in `anon_device`. With `device_limit` set, `Authenticate` now returns an error for any new device once the count is reached. An attacker can send `device_limit` requests with random header values and thereby block all legitimate new anonymous visitors; the fabricated rows stay counted for 30 days (`anonymousDeviceExpiration`) and there is no admin endpoint to delete devices (`/api/anonymous/devices` is read-only). This turns the limit into a trivial denial-of-service vector for anonymous access. At minimum the behaviour and the recovery path should be documented, and a delete/cleanup API or ID validation considered.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `tagDeviceUI` function populates the local cache with the device ID before the `CreateOrUpdateDevice` call. If `ErrDeviceLimitReached` is returned, the cache entry remains set, allowing subsequent requests to bypass the device limit until the cache expires after 29 minutes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Local cache is populated before the store write, so a device rejected by the limit is let through on its next request

`tagDeviceUI` calls `a.localCache.SetDefault(key, struct{}{})` before `a.anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice`. When the store returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, the error is propagated and `Anonymous.Authenticate` correctly refuses the request, but the device's cache key has already been written. On the very next request from the same `X-Grafana-Device-Id` (and for the next ~29 minutes), `tagDeviceUI` hits the cache and returns nil, so `Authenticate` succeeds and the device is served as a normal anonymous user even though it was never recorded and the limit is still exhausted. The device limit is therefore only enforced for a single request per device per cache lifetime. The cache entry must only be written after `CreateOrUpdateDevice` succeeds (or be deleted on `ErrDeviceLimitReached`).

false_negatives.golden_comment: The updateDevice function returns ErrDeviceLimitReached when rowsAffected == 0, but zero affected rows means the device doesn't exist or falls outside the time window, not that a limit was reached.

Time window calculation inconsistency: Using device.UpdatedAt.UTC().Add(-anonymousDeviceExpiration) as the lower bound but device.UpdatedAt as the current time may not match the intended logic. Consider using time.Now().UTC() consistently.

false_positives.candidate:
Device limit is bypassed by any request that omits the X-Grafana-Device-Id header

`TagDevice` returns nil immediately when the `X-Grafana-Device-Id` header is absent, and `Authenticate` then issues a full anonymous identity. Since the limit is only enforced inside `CreateOrUpdateDevice`, any client that does not send the header (curl, scripts, a browser with the header stripped) is never counted and is never blocked, even when the limit is reached. The new `device_limit` setting therefore cannot be relied on as an access cap; it only constrains well-behaved UI clients. This should be documented clearly for the setting, or non-UI anonymous requests should be handled explicitly when the limit is active.

No test covers the 'update existing device when limit reached' path or the client rejecting a new device

`TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit` only verifies that a second, new device is rejected. The new `updateDevice` branch (an already-counted device must still be refreshed when `count >= deviceLimit`, and a stale device outside the 30-day window must be rejected) is untested, as is the end-to-end behaviour in `Anonymous.Authenticate` returning an error on `ErrDeviceLimitReached` and the interaction with the local cache in `impl_test.go`. Given the limit now gates authentication, these paths should have coverage; a test for the cache interaction would have caught the bypass described for `tagDeviceUI`.

ProvideAnonDBStore now requires an int64 and ProvideAnonymousDeviceService no longer accepts an AnonStore; DI wiring must be updated

Before this change `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` received an `anonstore.AnonStore` from dependency injection, which implies `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore` (and a `wire.Bind` for `AnonStore`) is registered in `pkg/server/wire.go`. This PR changes `ProvideAnonDBStore` to take `(db.DB, int64)` and makes the service construct the store itself, but `wire.go`/`wire_gen.go` are not in the changed file set. If the provider is still listed, wire generation fails (no provider for `int64`, or an unused-provider error); if it has been silently dropped elsewhere, any other consumer of `anonstore.AnonStore` loses its provider. The wiring changes should be included in this PR and `make gen-go`/wire regenerated.

anonymousDeviceLimit is typed as `undefined` on GrafanaBootConfig and the backend never sends undefined

`anonymousDeviceLimit = undefined;` without an explicit type annotation gives the class field the static type `undefined` (not `number | undefined`), so consumers of `config.anonymousDeviceLimit` cannot use it as a number without a cast even though `merge(this, defaults, options)` assigns a number at runtime. Additionally, `FrontendSettingsDTO.AnonymousDeviceLimit` is a non-`omitempty` `int64`, so the backend always serialises a number (0 when the limit is disabled) and the `| undefined` in `GrafanaConfig` never occurs in practice. Declare it as `anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined = undefined;` (matching `loginError`) or type it as `number` with a 0 default, and make the DTO/TS types agree.

true_positives.golden_comment: The enableSqlExpressions function has flawed logic that always returns false, effectively disabling SQL expressions unconditionally:
true_positives.matched_candidate:
enableSqlExpressions computes an inverted, unused flag value

`enableSqlExpressions` assigns `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` — i.e. the variable named `enabled` is true when the feature toggle is OFF — and then returns `false` on both branches, so the toggle lookup is dead code. The net effect (always disabled) is what this PR intends, but the function is misleading: anyone later re-enabling the feature by changing the body to `return enabled` would enable SQL expressions exactly when the toggle is disabled and disable them when it is enabled. If the intent is to hard-disable regardless of the toggle, the function should simply return false (or be a constant) without the inverted lookup; if the toggle should be honored later, the negation must be removed.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The DB methods NewInMemoryDB().RunCommands, DB.QueryFramesInto, and DB.TablesList in pkg/expr/sql/db.go return hardcoded 'not implemented' errors after removing the go-duck dependency.

false_positives.candidate:
FlagSqlExpressions feature toggle remains registered and documented but can never enable the feature

After this change, SQL expressions are rejected unconditionally ("sqlExpressions is not implemented") regardless of the `sqlExpressions` feature toggle. The toggle remains in the feature registry and in the feature-toggle docs with no indication that it is now inert, so operators who enable it will get an error with no explanation. Either the toggle description/docs should state that the feature is disabled pending a secure re-implementation, or the toggle should be removed/marked as such, so users are not misled into thinking the flag still gates a working feature.

`CreateOrUpdateDevice` runs `CountDevices` in one DB session and the insert/upsert in a separate `WithDbSession` call, with no transaction or row locking. If several previously-unseen devices authenticate concurrently (or across multiple Grafana instances, which share the table but not the local cache), each sees `count < deviceLimit` and all of them insert, so the number of active devices can exceed `device_limit` by the degree of concurrency. If the limit is meant to be a hard cap (it blocks authentication), the check and insert should be performed in a single transaction, or the insert should be made conditional in SQL.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same race condition: concurrent requests can pass a non-atomic device count check and then insert devices beyond the configured limit. Both suggest transaction-based protection or locking.

true_positives.golden_comment: Anonymous authentication now fails entirely if anonDeviceService.TagDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached. Previously, device tagging was asynchronous and non-blocking. This change prevents anonymous users from authenticating when the device limit is reached.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unauthenticated callers can exhaust the device limit with arbitrary device IDs and lock out anonymous access for 30 days

`X-Grafana-Device-Id` is a client-supplied header with no validation, and each distinct value creates a row in `anon_device`. With `device_limit` set, `Authenticate` now returns an error for any new device once the count is reached. An attacker can send `device_limit` requests with random header values and thereby block all legitimate new anonymous visitors; the fabricated rows stay counted for 30 days (`anonymousDeviceExpiration`) and there is no admin endpoint to delete devices (`/api/anonymous/devices` is read-only). This turns the limit into a trivial denial-of-service vector for anonymous access. At minimum the behaviour and the recovery path should be documented, and a delete/cleanup API or ID validation considered.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same core regression: Authenticate now returns an error when the anonymous device limit is reached, blocking anonymous access. It expands on how an attacker could trigger the limit and prolong the lockout, but the underlying authentication failure matches the golden comment.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `tagDeviceUI` function populates the local cache with the device ID before the `CreateOrUpdateDevice` call. If `ErrDeviceLimitReached` is returned, the cache entry remains set, allowing subsequent requests to bypass the device limit until the cache expires after 29 minutes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Local cache is populated before the store write, so a device rejected by the limit is let through on its next request

`tagDeviceUI` calls `a.localCache.SetDefault(key, struct{}{})` before `a.anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice`. When the store returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, the error is propagated and `Anonymous.Authenticate` correctly refuses the request, but the device's cache key has already been written. On the very next request from the same `X-Grafana-Device-Id` (and for the next ~29 minutes), `tagDeviceUI` hits the cache and returns nil, so `Authenticate` succeeds and the device is served as a normal anonymous user even though it was never recorded and the limit is still exhausted. The device limit is therefore only enforced for a single request per device per cache lifetime. The cache entry must only be written after `CreateOrUpdateDevice` succeeds (or be deleted on `ErrDeviceLimitReached`).
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same cache-before-store bug: ErrDeviceLimitReached leaves the device ID cached, allowing subsequent requests to bypass the device limit for approximately 29 minutes.

false_positives.candidate:
Device limit is bypassed by any request that omits the X-Grafana-Device-Id header

`TagDevice` returns nil immediately when the `X-Grafana-Device-Id` header is absent, and `Authenticate` then issues a full anonymous identity. Since the limit is only enforced inside `CreateOrUpdateDevice`, any client that does not send the header (curl, scripts, a browser with the header stripped) is never counted and is never blocked, even when the limit is reached. The new `device_limit` setting therefore cannot be relied on as an access cap; it only constrains well-behaved UI clients. true_positives.matched_candidate:
align-items mixin forwards the modern keyword unchanged to legacy prefixes and emits a non-existent `-ms-align-items` property

`-webkit-box-align` (2009 model) and `-ms-flex-align` (IE10 2012 draft) accept `start`/`end`, not `flex-start`/`flex-end`; the mixin passes `$alignment` through verbatim, so any future `@include align-items(flex-start)` silently produces invalid declarations for those engines (only `center`/`baseline`, the values used today, happen to coincide). `float: right` on .small-action button is ignored now that .small-action is a flex container

`.small-action` is turned into a flex container via `@include flexbox()`, which makes `.topic-avatar`, `.small-action-desc` and `button` flex items. The CSS Flexbox spec states that `float` has no effect on flex items, so the `float: right` left on `button` (and `float: left` on `.topic-avatar`) no longer does anything. Because `.small-action-desc` has no `flex: 1`/width and the button has no `margin-left: auto`, the action button (e.g. the close/archive toggle) will now render immediately after the description text instead of at the right edge of the row — a visible layout regression for every small-action post. The button needs `margin-left: auto` (or the desc needs `flex: 1`) to restore the right alignment.

Right-alignment of .panel relies on `margin-left: auto`, which the legacy `-webkit-box` model emitted by the mixin does not honor

The `flexbox()` mixin deliberately emits `display: -webkit-box` / `-moz-box` for legacy WebKit/Gecko engines (Android stock browser < 4.4, Safari < 6.1, old Chrome). In the 2009 box model, auto margins are not used for distribution and `float` is ignored on box children, so with `float: right` removed and only `margin-left: auto` added, `.panel` (the icons/login buttons) will sit directly after the site title instead of at the right edge of the header on exactly the browsers the prefixes are meant to support. Either drop the legacy prefixes (and accept modern-flexbox-only), or add a legacy-compatible fallback such as `-webkit-box-flex: 1` on `.title`/`.extra-info-wrapper` or `-webkit-box-pack: justify` on `.contents`.

Float-based header layout removed with no fallback for browsers without any flexbox support

`.title { float: left }` and `.panel { float: right }` were deleted and replaced solely by flexbox on `.contents`. Browsers with no flexbox implementation at all (IE9 and older, Opera Mini) will now render `.title`, `.extra-info-wrapper` and `.panel` as stacked block elements, breaking the header entirely rather than degrading. If any such browser is still in the support matrix the floats should be kept as a fallback (flexbox ignores floats on flex items, so keeping them is harmless for flex-capable browsers).

.extra-info-wrapper as a flex item has `min-width: auto`, so long topic titles will push .panel out of the header

Now that `.contents` is a flex container, `.extra-info-wrapper` (which holds the docked topic title and category badge) becomes a flex item. Flex items default to `min-width: auto`, meaning they refuse to shrink below their content's min-content width. The wrapper gets `order(2)` but no `flex: 1 1 auto` / `min-width: 0` / `overflow: hidden`, so a long topic title (especially one with `white-space: nowrap`, as applied to `.badge-wrapper`) will widen the item and push `.panel` outside the header or wrap the row, instead of truncating as the previous float layout allowed. Add `min-width: 0; flex: 1;` (with `overflow: hidden`/ellipsis as desired) to the wrapper.

Removing paragraph margins in .custom-message collapses spacing between multi-paragraph messages `.small-action .small-action-desc .custom-message p` had `margin: 5px 0` and now has `margin: 0`. Custom close/archive/pin messages can contain multiple paragraphs (the message is cooked markdown), so consecutive `

A maintainer reading the history will be misled about why the header, small-action and badge layouts changed; the title/description should describe the actual change (float → flexbox layout, vendor-prefix mixins) and note the visual changes (removed bullet margin, small-action spacing).

true_positives.golden_comment: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
`<%- end if %>` is a typo that only compiles by accident

The closing tag of the header conditional is `<%- end if %>` instead of `<%- end %>`. Erubis emits `end if \n` followed by the next generated statement, so Ruby parses it as `(if ... else ... end) if @output_buffer.safe_append='...'` — a modifier-if whose condition is the whitespace-append statement for the following text node. It happens to be truthy so the template renders, but the output ordering is now dependent on surrounding whitespace and any reformatting of the template (e.g. removing the blank line, or an expression tag immediately following) turns this into a `SyntaxError` that 500s the whole embed endpoint. Replace with `<%- end %>`.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the erroneous `<%- end if %>` closing tag and recommend replacing it with `<%- end %>`. The candidate differs on when it causes a syntax error, but targets the same underlying ERB/Ruby issue.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
`i.content` is nil for ordinary RSS 2.0 feeds and `String#scrub` requires Ruby 2.1

SimpleRSS exposes Atom `<content>` as `item.content`; RSS 2.0 feeds that carry the body in `<description>` (or `<content:encoded>`, exposed as `content_encoded`) yield `i.content == nil`, so `i.content.scrub` raises `NoMethodError` on the very first item and the whole poll fails every hour for such feeds. Separately, `String#scrub` was only added in Ruby 2.1.0 (Dec 2013); this codebase still targets 1.9/2.0 (see the Gemfile comments), where the call raises `NoMethodError` even when content is present. Fall back through `content_encoded`/`description`/`summary`, skip items with no body, and avoid `scrub` or guard it with `respond_to?`.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same nil-content bug: RSS feeds may omit content, causing i.content.scrub to raise an exception, and recommends falling back to description. Its additional Ruby compatibility concern does not negate the match.

false_positives.candidate:
Unauthenticated users can trigger topic creation for arbitrary URLs on the embeddable host

`EmbedController#best` is reachable without login (`current_user` may be nil) and the only gate is a `Referer` header whose host equals `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`; `Referer` is trivially spoofed with curl. For any `embed_url` with no existing `TopicEmbed`, the action enqueues `retrieve_topic`, which (via `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` → `TopicEmbed.import_remote`) fetches the URL and creates a brand-new topic+post as the configured `embed_by_username` user. The redis throttle in `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` is keyed per exact URL, so an attacker can mint unlimited distinct URLs on the allowed host (`http://host/page?x=1`, `?x=2`, ..., or arbitrary ports `http://host:22/`) and have the forum crawl each one and publish a new topic for every variant with identical content. There is no per-client rate limit, no check that the URL path is one the site owner intends to embed, and no dedupe on fetched content. Consequence: anonymous topic flooding / forum spam and an outbound-fetch amplifier.

import_remote uses Kernel#open on a semi-trusted URL with no scheme check, timeout, size limit or redirect restriction

`TopicEmbed.import_remote` calls `open(url).read` (Kernel#open via open-uri) before `import` performs its `^https?://` check, so for the `TopicRetriever` path only the *host* of the URL has been validated. open-uri will follow HTTP redirects to any host, so a page on the embeddable host (or an attacker who can place redirects there) can make the forum fetch internal/other-host resources; there is also no read timeout and no size cap, so a slow or huge response ties up or exhausts a Sidekiq worker. Validate the scheme up front, use an explicit HTTP client with timeouts, a maximum body size, and either disable redirects or re-validate the host on each hop.

`post.present?` is the wrong success check for PostCreator; failures surface as NOT NULL violations and abort the import

`PostCreator#create` returns the unsaved `Post` object (with `errors` populated) when it rolls back, e.g. when `rollback_if_host_spam_detected` fires. `post.present?` is therefore true even on failure, and the code proceeds to `TopicEmbed.create!(post_id: post.id)` with `post.id == nil`, which hits the `post_id NOT NULL` constraint and raises a `PG::NotNullViolation` out of `import`. This is not a remote edge case: the configured `embed_by_username` user is typically a freshly created bot account at trust level 0, every imported post links to the same external host (the 'Imported from' footer alone guarantees this), and `Post#has_host_spam?` blocks TL0 users after `newuser_spam_host_threshold` (3) posts to the same domain. After the third import every subsequent import raises, the hourly `PollFeed` run aborts on the first item, and moderators receive spam-blocked PMs. Note also that the inner `Post.transaction` in `PostCreator` swallows `ActiveRecord::Rollback` because it is nested in `Topic.transaction` without `requires_new`, so relying on the rollback to clean up is fragile. Check `post.persisted?`/`post.errors.blank?` and either bypass or handle spam/rate-limit checks for the importer user.

absolutize_urls mangles protocol-relative URLs (//cdn.example.com/...) Both the `` and `` branches treat anything starting with `/` as site-relative and rewrite it to `"#{prefix}/#{href.sub(/^\/+/, '')}"`. A protocol-relative URL such as `//cdn.example.com/img.png` (very common in WordPress and other feeds) therefore becomes `http://embeddable-host/cdn.example.com/img.png`, which is a broken link/image in every imported post. Only rewrite when the value starts with a single `/` (or use `URI.join(url, href)` which handles all relative forms correctly).

Port is omitted/added based on hardcoded 80/443 instead of the scheme's default port

`prefix << ":#{uri.port}" if uri.port != 80 && uri.port != 443` drops the port for `https://host:80/` and `http://host:443/`, producing a prefix that points at the wrong port for those (unusual but valid) URLs. Use `uri.port != uri.default_port` so the port is kept exactly when it differs from the scheme default.

Re-import of an existing embed crashes if the post was deleted

When a `TopicEmbed` row exists, `embed.post` is used unconditionally. `Post` includes `Trashable`, so a post that has been deleted (trashed) is excluded by the default scope and `embed.post` returns nil; `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!` then raises `NoMethodError` on the next feed poll or retrieve, and since `PollFeed` has no per-item error handling this aborts the whole feed run every hour until the row is removed by hand. Guard for a missing post (skip, or recreate the topic) and consider cleaning up `topic_embeds` when the topic/post is destroyed.

No per-item error handling: one bad item (or the post rate limiter) aborts the whole feed

The `rss.items.each` loop calls `TopicEmbed.import` with no rescue. Any exception for a single item — malformed `URI`, nil title, the `PostCreator` spam/NOT NULL failure described elsewhere, or `RateLimiter::LimitExceeded` — propagates, `sidekiq_options retry: false` means the job is not retried, and all remaining items are skipped. In particular `Post` declares `rate_limit` (`rate_limit_create_post`, `max_topics_per_day: 20`); unless `embed_by_username` is staff, importing a feed with more than 20 items raises `LimitExceeded` partway through on every run, and `rate_limit_create_post` (5s between posts) will trip on consecutive items. The Disqus thor task explicitly calls `RateLimiter.disable` for the same reason; the job should do likewise (or use a staff-only importer) and wrap each item in a rescue that logs and continues.

Feed HTML is stored and rendered completely unsanitized

`CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content)` is passed straight to `TopicEmbed.import`, which stores it as a `raw_html` post; `Post#cook` returns `raw` verbatim for that cook method, so no sanitizer (PrettyText/Sanitize) ever runs on it. Unlike `import_remote`, which at least passes content through Readability's tag/attribute whitelist, the RSS path lets `<script>`, event handlers, `javascript:` hrefs, iframes etc. from the feed land in `cooked` and execute for every visitor of the forum and of the embed iframe. A compromised blog, a third-party/aggregated feed, or an author-submitted post on a multi-author site becomes site-wide stored XSS on the forum. Run feed content through the same whitelist used for Readability (or Sanitize) before storing.

Throttle key set with SETNX then EXPIRE non-atomically

`$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by a separate `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)` is not atomic. If the worker dies or the Redis connection drops between the two calls, the key persists with no TTL and `retrieved_recently?` returns true forever for that URL, so non-staff visitors can never trigger retrieval of that embed again. Use `SET key 1 NX EX 60` (or `setex` inside a MULTI) so the TTL is applied in the same operation.

Every retrieval of an unknown URL synchronously re-polls and re-imports the entire RSS feed

When `feed_polling_enabled` is on, `perform_retrieve` runs `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline, which downloads and parses the whole feed and calls `TopicEmbed.import` for every item (each doing a DB lookup, SHA1, Nokogiri parse) before falling back to `fetch_http`. Because `embed/best` enqueues a retrieval for every unknown `embed_url` and the throttle is per-URL, a handful of visitors hitting distinct not-yet-embedded pages (or an attacker varying the query string) causes repeated full feed re-imports on the Sidekiq workers. Consider only consulting the already-scheduled hourly poll results, or at minimum throttling the feed poll itself globally.

Disqus import silently drops the --category option and original topic timestamps

The `category` method_option was removed and the topic is now created via `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, which no longer passes `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])` or a category. Imported threads will all appear in the uncategorized category with the import time as their creation date (and therefore sort as brand-new), and anyone invoking the task with `-c` will get a Thor 'unknown option' error. If this is intentional it should be mentioned; otherwise thread `created_at`/`category` through `import_remote`/`import` opts to `PostCreator`.

Key authorization and parsing paths are untested

The controller spec only covers 'no referer'; there is no test that a referer on a *different* host is rejected, which is the actual security property of `ensure_embeddable`. Likewise `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb` never exercises `poll_feed` itself (nil `content`, non-http `link` falling back to `id`), and `spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb` has no cases for protocol-relative URLs, non-default ports, or the update path when the post has been deleted — all of which have concrete bugs in this PR. Add tests for referer-host mismatch, a feed item without `content`, and `absolutize_urls` with `//host/path` input.

`ruby-readability` and `simple-rss` are added unconditionally to the Gemfile, but only `Gemfile_rails4.lock` was regenerated. Booting with `RAILS3=1` resolves against `Gemfile.lock`, which no longer matches the Gemfile; in deployment/frozen mode `bundle install` fails, and in normal mode the lockfile is silently rewritten with potentially different versions. Either regenerate `Gemfile.lock` as well or scope the gems to the rails4 branch.

`prisma` is used but never imported in Salesforce CalendarService

The new refresh block in `getClient` calls `await prisma.credential.update(...)`, but this file has no `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma"` (imports are only jsforce, rrule, zod, lib helpers and types). This is a type-check error and, if it slipped through, a `ReferenceError: prisma is not defined` at runtime on every Salesforce service instantiation, making the Salesforce integration unusable.

Request to the self-hoster's credential sync endpoint carries no authentication

The POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` in the body with no secret/signature header (e.g. `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` under `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME`, which the inbound webhook already requires). The endpoint returns live OAuth access tokens for arbitrary user ids, so the self-hoster is forced to either leave it unauthenticated (anyone who can reach it can obtain any user's third-party tokens by guessing numeric ids) or rely on network-level controls. The outgoing request should include the shared secret so the endpoint can verify the caller.

Zoom sends app slug "zoomvideo" to the sync endpoint, but the app's slug is "zoom"

The inbound webhook (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`) looks apps up by their store slug, and Zoom's slug is `zoom` (see `zoomvideo/api/callback.ts` creating the credential with `appId: "zoom"`). The refresh path, however, calls `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoomvideo", ...)`. A self-hoster keying their endpoint by the same slugs they use for the webhook will not recognize `zoomvideo`, so Zoom token refresh via sync fails. Use the canonical slug `zoom` to match the rest of the system.

Webhook upserts by (userId, appId) and will silently overwrite an arbitrary credential when a user has several for the same app

Cal.com allows multiple credentials per user for the same app (e.g. several Google Calendar accounts, each a separate `Credential` row with `appId: "google-calendar"`). The handler does `findFirst({ where: { userId, appId } })` with no ordering and overwrites whichever row is returned, so a sync for one connected account can clobber the keys of a different one, breaking that calendar connection. It also never considers team-owned credentials. The payload should identify the target credential (e.g. a credential id or an external account identifier), or the handler should refuse/branch when more than one match exists.

Helper throws on invalid response, making callers' `!success` branches dead and changing Office365 error behavior

`parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws `"Invalid refreshed tokens were returned"` when validation fails, so the `if (!parsedToken.success)` checks in `zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts` and `salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts` can never execute. For Office365 this silently changes behavior: the previous code logged the Zod error together with Microsoft's raw response and continued; now the diagnostic logging was deleted and the refresh throws, leaving operators with no information about why Microsoft's response was rejected. Either return the failed result and let callers handle it, or keep the diagnostic logging in the helper.

No tests for the new webhook or the shared refresh helpers

The PR adds a new authenticated API endpoint that writes third-party credentials to the DB and two helpers (`refreshOAuthTokens`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse`) that are now on the token-refresh path of ten integrations, yet ships no unit or integration tests (the PR checklist explicitly says none were added). Several of the defects above (SafeParse wrapper stored as key, broken computed-key schema, Response vs SDK shape mismatch, missing prisma import) would have been caught by even a basic test of each helper's output shape and of one adapter's refresh flow in both sync and non-sync modes.
